outcomes.text: Explain the purpose of the CPU.
Describe what happens at each stage of the fetch-execute cycle.
Explain the role of the ALU, control unit, cache and registers, and what each manages during the cycle.
Describe the Von Neumann architecture and what the MAR, MDR, program counter and accumulator each store (data versus address).
Explain how clock speed, cache size and number of cores affect CPU performance, alone or in combination.
Explain what an embedded system is and give examples.
Describe typical characteristics of embedded systems.
Explain why computers need primary storage and what it usually consists of.
Describe the purpose and key characteristics of RAM and ROM and how they differ.
Explain what virtual memory is, why it is needed and how data moves between RAM and secondary storage.
Describe the role of cache memory.
Explain why computers need secondary storage.
Recognise optical, magnetic and solid state storage and compare them on capacity, speed, portability, durability, reliability and cost.
Choose suitable storage devices and media for a given scenario.
Explain why data must be stored in binary and how data is converted to binary for processing.
Use the units bit, nibble, byte, KB, MB, GB, TB and PB and convert between them.
Calculate the storage capacity needed for a set of files.
Calculate sound, image and text file sizes from their formulas.
Convert positive whole numbers between denary and binary (up to 8 bits).
Add two 8-bit binary integers and explain overflow errors.
Convert between denary and 2-digit hexadecimal.
Convert between binary and hexadecimal.
Carry out binary shifts left and right and describe their effect on a number.
Explain how characters are represented in binary, including character sets and how bits per character limit the number of characters (ASCII, Unicode).
Explain how an image is stored as pixels and how colour depth and resolution affect its quality and size, including metadata.
Explain how sound is sampled and stored digitally and how sample rate, duration and bit depth affect quality and file size.
Explain why compression is needed.
Compare lossy and lossless compression, including their advantages, disadvantages and effects on files.
Describe LANs and WANs and the factors that affect network performance.
Contrast client-server and peer-to-peer networks.
Describe the hardware that links computers into a LAN: wireless access points, routers, switches, NICs and transmission media.
Explain the Internet as a network of networks, including DNS, hosting, web servers and clients, and the Cloud with its pros and cons.
Compare star and mesh topologies.
Compare wired (Ethernet) and wireless (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth) connections and recommend one for a scenario.
Explain the principle of encryption for securing network data.
Describe IP addressing (IPv4, IPv6) and MAC addressing.
Explain what standards are and why they let hardware and software from different makers work together.
Describe the purpose of common protocols: TCP/IP, HTTP, HTTPS, FTP, POP, IMAP and SMTP.
Explain how protocols use layers and the benefits of layering.
Describe how and why malware, social engineering (such as phishing), brute-force attacks, denial of service, data interception and theft, and SQL injection are carried out.
Explain how penetration testing, anti-malware, firewalls, user access levels, passwords, encryption and physical security limit threats.
Describe the purpose of an operating system and its user interface.
Explain memory management and how it allows multitasking.
Explain peripheral management and drivers.
Describe user management, including accounts, access rights and security.
Describe file management: naming, folders, moving and saving files.
Explain what utility software is and why it is needed beyond the operating system.
Describe the purpose of encryption, defragmentation and data compression software.

topics.title: 1.6 Ethical, legal, cultural and environmental impacts of digital technology

outcomes.text: Discuss ethical, legal, cultural, environmental and privacy impacts of digital technology on society using examples.
Describe the Data Protection Act 2018, the Computer Misuse Act 1990 and the Copyright Designs and Patents Act 1988, and what each allows or prohibits.
Explain why software needs licences and compare open source and proprietary licences, recommending one for a scenario.

units.title: Component 02: Computational thinking, algorithms and programming

outcomes.text: Explain abstraction, decomposition and algorithmic thinking and how they define and refine problems.
Identify the inputs, processes and outputs of a problem.
Draw structure diagrams showing a problem's subsections and links.
Create, interpret, complete and correct algorithms in pseudocode, flowcharts and a programming language, including nesting.
Identify syntax and logic errors and suggest fixes.
Use trace tables to follow an algorithm.
Explain and apply binary search and linear search, including their prerequisites.
Explain and apply bubble sort, merge sort and insertion sort to a data set.
Identify a standard algorithm from its code or pseudocode.
Use variables, constants, inputs, outputs and assignments.
Use sequence, selection and iteration (count- and condition-controlled loops).
Use comparison and arithmetic operators, including MOD, DIV and exponentiation.
Use the Boolean operators AND, OR and NOT in programs.
Use integer, real, Boolean, character and string data types and choose suitable ones for a scenario.
Explain and use casting to change a data type.
Manipulate strings using concatenation and slicing.
Open, read, write and close files.
Use 1D and 2D arrays and records to store data.
Use SQL SELECT, FROM and WHERE to search for data.
Write functions and procedures with local and global variables and array passing.
Generate and use random numbers.
Anticipate misuse and invalid inputs when designing programs.
Design input validation and simple authentication such as username and password.
Make code maintainable with sub programs, naming conventions, indentation and comments.
Explain the purpose of testing and distinguish iterative from final testing.
Identify syntax errors and logic errors.
Choose normal, boundary, invalid and erroneous test data and complete a test plan.
Refine algorithms after testing.
Recognise AND, OR and NOT gate symbols and complete their truth tables.
Create, complete and edit logic diagrams and truth tables, combining several gates, to solve problems.

topics.title: 2.5 Programming languages and Integrated Development Environments

outcomes.text: Distinguish high-level from low-level languages and explain why translators are needed.
Compare compilers and interpreters, with benefits and drawbacks.
Describe IDE tools (editors, error diagnostics, run-time environment, translators) and how they help a programmer.
